subject: Scaling hosted plan for Q3 surge
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-retail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.c@acme-retail.com>
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scaling hosted plan for Q3 surge

Hi Mina,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week — the team found the batching and KV-cache explanations really helpful. We're projecting a 3x traffic spike across checkout recommendations starting in July (marketing + gift season). Before the exec review on Friday, procurement asked for a clear path to avoid throttles and to estimate committed spend.

Quick numbers from our side: current monthly hosted commit ~ 1.2M tokens; expected steady-state July–Sep ~ 3.6M tokens, with short bursts to ~5M. We care about keeping p95 generation latency < 220ms and avoiding soft-throttle windows.

Can you send a proposal that includes:
- recommended monthly commit for Q3 (and a staged ramp if helpful)
- slot for burst capacity / burst minutes and how billing is handled during bursts
- any suggested rate limits or soft-throttle guardrails we should expect
- estimated per-token pricing at each tier (including any commitment discounts)

Attaching our March usage export. Procure may also want a formal SOW and a DocuSign link. CC'ing Alyssa from ops and procurement email for visibility.

Thanks,
Jordan

-- 
Jordan Ellis
Head of Infrastructure, Acme Retail
jordan.ellis@acme-retail.com
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.c@acme-retail.com>, procure@acme-retail.com
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2029 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scaling hosted plan for Q3 surge

Jordan — really appreciate the detailed numbers, that makes this straightforward. Summary response below and attaching our hosted ratecard + a draft SOW for a 6-month ramp.

Short summary recommendations:
- Staged monthly commit: 1.5M (May), 2.5M (June), 3.6M (July–Sep)
- Burst cushion: additional 2.0M tokens/month pool for short windows (billed only when used; reserve at 24-48h notice for guaranteed capacity)
- Soft-throttle policy: gradual throughput backoff at 90% of committed QPS for sustained 60s; we can configure a hard fallback to a lower-cost model if desired
- Discounts: 10% off list token rate for a 6-month commit at 3.6M+; 14% for 12-months (pricing detail in attachment)

Operational notes:
- To meet p95 < 220ms we recommend pinning the model variant we tested and enabling prefix KV caching for your common checkout prompts.
- We'll provide a 48-hour canary window before the full ramp to validate latency under real load.

Next steps I propose:
1) Your ops team approves the ramp dates (June 1 and July 1 as primary targets)
2) Procurement confirms acceptable billing cadence and we exchange a redlineable SOW
3) We'll schedule the 48-hour canary and share runbooks

Attaching: redwood_hosted_ratecard_v4.pdf, draft_SOW_ACME_MonthlyCommit_v1.pdf

Happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow if that helps.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Account Executive — Hosted
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2029 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Scaling hosted plan for Q3 surge — Acme proposal (internal)

Ben/Karthik — forwarding Acme thread. They want a staged ramp to ~3.6M tokens/mo with burst cushion and a canary. Key asks for internal decision:

- Pricing: they asked for a 10% committment discount for 6 months (3.6M), possible 14% for 12 months. My draft uses 10% for 6mo with a 2.0M burst bucket billed on usage.
- Ops: we need to confirm SLA & p95 target — ops told me p95 < 220ms plausible if we pin model variant + KV cache. Any objections to offering the 48-hour guaranteed canary window?
- Throttle behavior: recommend we offer a soft backoff at sustained 90% QPS and an automatic fallback to a quantized variant if we detect persistent overload. Need product sign-off on the fallback model and tracking for quality regressions.

Draft commercial bullets for Acme (for approval):
• Staged monthly commits: May 1 = 1.5M, Jun 1 = 2.5M, Jul 1 = 3.6M/month (Q3)
• Burst pool: 2.0M tokens/month (one-time useable, billed on consumption)
• Discount: 10% off list token rate for 6-month term; billing monthly in arrears
• Canary: guaranteed 48h warm-up/canary before July ramp; ops-led runbook
• Fallback: automatic model variant degrade with quality monitoring and rollback hooks

Can you both review and confirm and then I can send the redline SOW to procurement and DocuSign link to Jordan?

Thanks,
Mina
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Apr 2029 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Scaling hosted plan for Q3 surge — Acme proposal (internal)

Mina — looks good to me. A few notes:
- Approve 10% for 6 months; we should hold 12% as stretch to negotiate if they push for a longer term.
- Canary: approve 48h guaranteed but add a clause that full SLA/latency targets start after successful canary validation (we'll define pass conditions in the runbook).
- Burst pool billing: suggest we bill burst consumption at list rate (no discount) to discourage heavy sustained usage; this should be clear in SOW.
- Add a clause about a 30-day review after first month of Q3 to measure KV cache hit-rate and consider adjusting commit up/down.

Once Karthik signs off on the fallback model (quality delta acceptable) we can send the SOW + DocuSign.

—Ben
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.c@acme-retail.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, procure@acme-retail.com
Date: Wed, 10 Apr 2029 15:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Scaling hosted plan for Q3 surge

Jordan — looping in Ben and Karthik for final commercial & ops sign-off. Per our internal review we can proceed with the staged ramp and 48-hour canary with the following confirmed items:

- Staged commits: May 1 = 1.5M, Jun 1 = 2.5M, Jul 1 = 3.6M/month (Q3).
- Burst: 2.0M token cushion per month, billed on consumption at list rate.
- Discount: 10% off list token rate for the 6-month commitment (Mar–Aug window), applied to committed tokens only.
- Canary: 48-hour validation window; SLA targets enforced after canary passes; runbook to be shared with ops.
- Fallback: automatic switch to a quantized variant if sustained overload detected; we'll include quality-monitoring gates and an automatic rollback path.

I've attached the redline-friendly SOW (ACME_MonthlyCommit_SOW_v1.pdf) and included a DocuSign link below for procurement to review and approve. Please confirm whether June 1 and July 1 dates work for you and whether procurement wants monthly billing in arrears or net-30 invoicing.

DocuSign: https://docusign.example.com/sender?doc=ACME_MonthlyCommit_SOW_v1

If you confirm today, we can target the May 1 partial uplift and schedule the 48-hour canary the week of June 24.

Best regards,
